steps.title: The lonely product
steps.prompt:
An INNER JOIN throws away rows without a partner.
LEFT JOIN keeps every row of the LEFT table, even partnerless ones.
Find the product nobody ever sold: its sale_items row just won't exist (NULL).
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT p.name, si.sale_id FROM products p LEFT JOIN sale_items si ON si.product_id = p.id WHERE si.sale_id IS NULL;
hints: Products are the LEFT table here.
A never-sold product has no sale_items row.
Write the LEFT JOIN with WHERE si.sale_id IS NULL.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, si.sale_id FROM products p LEFT JOIN sale_items si ON si.product_id = p.id WHERE si.sale_id IS NULL;
steps.memory_trick: LEFT JOIN = 'keep everyone on the left side'.

steps.title: The twenty quiet customers
steps.prompt:
Same trick, new heroes: which customers have never ordered?
Their sales row is missing.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT c.name, s.id AS sale_id FROM customers c LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.customer_id = c.id WHERE s.id IS NULL;
hints: Customers go LEFT, sales go RIGHT.
Keep only the rows where s.id is missing.
Write the LEFT JOIN and filter with WHERE s.id IS NULL.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT c.name, s.id AS sale_id FROM customers c LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.customer_id = c.id WHERE s.id IS NULL;
steps.memory_trick: AS gives a column a nicer name for reading.

steps.title: What does LEFT mean?
steps.prompt:
In FROM customers c LEFT JOIN sales s, every customer is kept - even ones with no sales.
A customer with no sales shows NULL for the sales columns. INNER JOIN would hide those rows entirely.
steps.task: Which table's rows are ALL kept by a LEFT JOIN?
hints: 'LEFT' points at the first table written.
In FROM customers c LEFT JOIN sales s, it's customers.
steps.memory_trick: LEFT = love your left table unconditionally.

steps.title: Predict: INNER vs LEFT
steps.task: How many rows (products with at least one sale)?
steps.memory_trick: INNER drops the lonely; LEFT keeps them.
